key_insight: The paper proposes a hybrid traffic-control framework that combines model-based prediction and multi-agent learning to coordinate lane-level speed limits and ramp metering on complex weaving segments while accounting for merging/diverging risk.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, lane-level active traffic management strategy for urban expressways, aiming to reduce congestion and collision risk with better adaptability than pure optimization or pure reinforcement learning.
method: Reconstruct lane-level L-METANET to model free/forced lane changes and flow redistribution.
Use XGBoost-SHAP plus random-parameters binary logit to quantify merging/diverging collision risks and define control rewards/costs.
Deploy MPC-STMAPPO: an MPC upper layer for long-horizon baseline actions and a Mamba+graph-attention MAPPO lower layer for residual short-horizon refinement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports real-world validation on the 18-km Eastern Expressway in Changchun, with accurate state reproduction, AUCs above 0.80 for most risk tasks, faster convergence, and stronger performance than MPC, MARL, and pure MARL baselines under fluctuating demand.
watch_item: Deployment will depend on reliable lane-level sensing, accurate calibration of the traffic and risk models, and safe online integration of RL residual actions with MPC constraints.
paper_title: Coordinated Lane-Level Variable Speed Limits and Ramp Metering for Successive Weaving Segments Considering Merging/Diverging Risks: A Hybrid Model Predictive Control and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
